searchText: This channel seems like it could be archived since development has shifted towards Verkle stuff. Sounds good to me! BTW we should have a more active discussion in how storage and code and account objects should be converted into Verkle tree keys I'm strongly in favor of mapping everything into a single tree if at all possible, or if we have to have a two-layer structure, have just a two-layer structure, don't have this weird "header in the middle" Agreed, unifying it *all* into a single layer structure sounds ideal, especially from my vantage point looking at things from a distributed storage network angle. By all I mean accounts, storage, and *maybe* the code trie. I say *definitely* the code trie I only say maybe because I haven't thought about it much so I was assuming there might be dragons hiding there. hmm the only dragon I can think of is that if we use the wrong map-to-key function then witnesses for N code chunks might be like 96 * N + 48 instead of just 48 But that's easy to avoid The main sacrifice with a single layer that I see is that it would require either generalized branch nodes (like the current hexary tree has), or a restricted version of branch node that goes up to multiples of 32 bytes Yeah, code chunks should be able to be normalized/compressed using high level understanding of what the data represents, rather than naive 1:1 mapping of the trie keys/data Oh I don't even mean that; I think a naive `chunks[i] = code[31*i: 31*(i+1)]` is totally fine We just want to avoid `chunks[hash(i)] = code[31*i: 31*(i+1)]` Oh sorry, add in 5 bits for "where does the pushdata end" a key scheme that allows for code chunks to be stored contiguously in the trie? right Basically, the desiderata for a key scheme are: * Unexploitability for accounts (can't force an account to have a length-N branch without 256**N work) * Unexploitability for storage keys * Contiguous code storage And I think we can have all that.... so something like the first chunk being at `hash(epoch | account | "code")` and subsequent chunks being at `hash(epoch | account | "code") + i`? maybe less confusing, first chunk is at `hash(<something-that-gives-us-a-random-unique-starting-point>)` and subsequent chunks being at `<first-chunk-key> + i` yeah I think that can work My intuition is that total number of chunks is limited enough that it allows for that contiguous address space without any meaningful increase in collision likelihood

excerpts.content: I'm strongly in favor of mapping everything into a single tree if at all possible, or if we have to have a two-layer structure, have just a two-layer structure, don't have this weird "header in the middle"

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: Agreed, unifying it *all* into a single layer structure sounds ideal, especially from my vantage point looking at things from a distributed storage network angle.

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: By all I mean accounts, storage, and *maybe* the code trie.

excerpts.content: I say *definitely* the code trie

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: I only say maybe because I haven't thought about it much so I was assuming there might be dragons hiding there.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: hmm the only dragon I can think of is that if we use the wrong map-to-key function then witnesses for N code chunks might be like 96 * N + 48 instead of just 48

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: But that's easy to avoid

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: The main sacrifice with a single layer that I see is that it would require either generalized branch nodes (like the current hexary tree has), or a restricted version of branch node that goes up to multiples of 32 bytes

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: Yeah, code chunks should be able to be normalized/compressed using high level understanding of what the data represents, rather than naive 1:1 mapping of the trie keys/data

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Oh I don't even mean that; I think a naive `chunks[i] = code[31*i: 31*(i+1)]`  is totally fine

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: We just want to avoid `chunks[hash(i)] = code[31*i: 31*(i+1)]`

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Oh sorry, add in 5 bits for "where does the pushdata end"

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: a key scheme that allows for code chunks to be stored contiguously in the trie?

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: right

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
Basically, the desiderata for a key scheme are:

* Unexploitability for accounts (can't force an account to have a length-N branch without 256**N work)
* Unexploitability for storage keys
* Contiguous code storage

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: And I think we can have all that....

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: so something like the first chunk being at `hash(epoch | account | "code")` and subsequent chunks being at `hash(epoch | account | "code") + i`?

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: maybe less confusing, first chunk is at `hash(<something-that-gives-us-a-random-unique-starting-point>)` and subsequent chunks being at `<first-chunk-key> + i`

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: yeah I think that can work
